jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Nursing
jobs.description: Assistant Professor of Nursing Print Assistant Professor of Nursing Salary $74,000.00 Annually Location Main Campus - 225 S University Ave, St. George 84770, UT Job Type Full-Time Faculty Job Number 27FAC970-1 Division College of Health Sciences Department Nursing Opening Date 06/16/2026 Closing Date Continuous Description Benefits Questions Position Announcement The Department of Nursing at Utah Tech University (UT) in St. George, Utah, invites applications for a full-time tenure-track Assistant Professor in Nursing position, starting Fall Semester 2026. The department, located in the state-of-the-art Taylor Health Sciences building (adjacent to St. George Regional Medical Center), offers a certified nursing certification, as well as associate, baccalaureate, and masters degrees in Nursing. More information about the department, faculty, and its degree offerings can be found online at https://health.utahtech.edu/nursing/. Responsibilities Teach a varied number of semester hours that includes lecture and laboratory annually and provide clinical supervision as assigned.May have direct assignments in the LPN, BSN and/or MSN programs.Develop nursing curriculum with measurable objectives for each course.Assist in the development and continued assessment of an excellent nursing program.Assist in ongoing efforts of all aspects of national accreditation, including self-report, onsite visits, follow-up, and ongoing evaluation of health programs.Plan, promote, and coordinate clinical contracts, clinical experiences, cooperative education and internships.Assist with student recruitment, advisement, placement, and follow-up efforts.Improve professionally and maintain currency in the field.Serve on college and department committees as assigned.Attend department, division, and faculty meetings and adhere to college policies.Assist nursing leadership and division dean, and perform other duties as assigned. Qualifications A Master's degree in Nursing required, doctorate degree or enrollment in a doctorate degree required.Two years of clinical experience and/or teaching in psychiatric nursing, transcultural nursing, pharmacology, professional nursing roles, and/or medical-surgical nursing required.Ability to team teach in classroom and lab, and facilitate students in clinical situations which may include day, night, or weekend classes.Must hold current Registered Nurse License for the state of Utah or eligibility to gain Utah Licensure.Ability to develop innovative curricula.Knowledge of subject matter, appropriate course content, current trends and methodologies in education and nursing.Knowledge of computer-based technology as used in clinical and educational environments including online teaching/learning environments.Knowledge of infection control issues and procedures.Strong organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills.Ability to represent well the Nursing Program and Utah Tech University. Supplemental Information POSITION DETAILS, COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS: Full-time (9-month) tenure-track faculty position. Faculty service begins fall semester 2026. Annual salary of $74,000, with additional compensation available for optional summer/overload teaching. Excellent benefits package included that begins on start date; includes medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance, employee assistance and wellness programs, retirement plan contributions, and undergraduate tuition waivers for employees and eligible dependents. See https://humanresources.utahtech.edu/employee-benefits/ under "Benefits Summary" for more details.ELECTRONIC APPLICATION PROCEDURES: Application review begins July 20, 2028; position open until filled.?Candidates must submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, contact information for three professional references (including email addresses), transcripts, and a Student Success Statement (1-2 pages about the candidate’s teaching or other professional experience working with a wide range of student academic preparedness). Please upload all the requested documents when you submit your application. Employment is contingent upon successful completion and certification of required degrees and upon successfully passing a background check.ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY: Utah Tech University is an open, comprehensive, polytechnic institution, committed to exceptional student learning and success that has adopted an instructional approach of "active learning. active life." and a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship. The area is renowned for its red rocks, desert climate, over 300 days of sunshine annually, and featuring easy access to world-class outdoor recreational opportunities. Click here to learn more about the University.Utah Tech University is a fast-growing Utah public institution of higher education, with more than 13,000 students. We offer over 250 programs, including doctoral, masters, bachelors, associates, certificates, endorsements, minors, and/or emphases. We seek faculty and staff committed to creating an active, applied, and career-oriented learning environment that is student-centered, who bring new ideas, possess values and career aspirations aligned with the University’s mission and vision, and are inspired to build a premier open, comprehensive, polytechnic university. Utah Tech employs only U.S. citizens and lawfully authorized non-U.S. citizens. All new employees must provide employment eligibility verification as required by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.Utah Tech is committed to providing access and reasonable accommodations in its services, programs, activities, education, and employment for individuals with disabilities. jobs.title: Dean of Students
jobs.description: Dean of Students Welcome from the Dean of Students Welcome to Westminster University. Whether you’re a currently enrolled student, an alum, or a family member or friend supporting a student, we are glad to have you as a part of our community. I can attest that Westminster is a very special place. It’s certainly a beautiful campus and our location in the Salt Lake valley is a great launching point for urban and wilderness adventures, but what truly makes Westminster special is the people: the students, staff, faculty, and the families and friends that together form a community of learners that genuinely care about each other and about making a difference in the world. While you’re here, I encourage you to lean into new experiences: Snag a free ticket to a performing arts event Enjoy a snack at the University-sponsored tailgate before cheering on one of our athletics teams Attend one of the many free lectures featuring world-renowned thought leaders that will challenge you to think differently As an institution of higher learning, Westminster wants to support and celebrate the growth you’ll experience while here. Maximizing your time at Westminster will require you to take [appropriate] risks, ask for help when needed, and offer help to others when you’re able. My role as the Dean of Students, and the purpose of our office, is to advocate for you and support your success. We can't wait to meet you soon. Go Griffins! Learn More About Student Care Student Care Navigating the college experience can be one of the most rewarding and challenging times in a student’s life. One of the best skills a student can learn while attending college is: How to advocate for themselves How to identify and access resources to support their well-being If you or someone you know is experiencing difficulties while attending Westminster, there are resources on campus to help. Integrated Wellness Students can access medical and mental health services in person with Integrated Wellness or online through Westminster's partnership with TimelyCare. The Purple Basket The Purple Basket addresses the impact of hunger, nutrition, housing insecurity, and disparities in access to basic needs. Students can access a variety of foods, as well as hygiene and household items, in the Purple Basket. If you're facing food insecurity and need additional support, you can find a list of local food resource centers. Submit a Report If you or someone you know may be experiencing a Title IX violation, you can submit a Title IX Incident Report. If you're concerned about another student, you can submit a Concerning Behavior Referral to alert a campus representative. Student Code of Conduct The Student Code of Conduct is updated annually and contains the institution's standards of behavior designed to uphold our pillars of honesty, reason, and respect. Read the Student Code of Conduct Title IX Westminster’s Title IX program is comprehensive and seeks to stop, remedy, and prevent incidents of gender-based discrimination and sexual misconduct. If you or someone you know may be experiencing a Title IX violation, this page will connect you to resources and the reporting form. Learn More About Title IX Parent and Family Resources If you are a member of a student’s support network, this page will connect you with monthly correspondence from the dean, as well as other useful campus resources for parents and families. Find Parent and Family Resources Institutional Safety Reporting As mandated by state and federal law, Westminster provides records of annual safety reports. View Institutional Safety Reporting Hazing Reporting View the latest federally-mandated Hazing Transparency Report. Report Hazing Drug and Alcohol Abuse Prevention Program Westminster provides a federally-mandated biennial DAAPP report. View DAAPP Reporting Dean's Advisory Council The Dean's Advisory Council (DAC) is a group of student leaders who work with the Dean of Students to create opportunities for strengthening the campus community and tackle issues that impact the student experience. DAC representatives serve as ambassadors for their fellow students, and their perspectives and input are highly valued and appreciated by the dean. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Any currently enrolled undergraduate or graduate student in good academic standing is eligible to serve on the DAC. Representatives are asked to attend 1 in-person meeting each month, attend events sponsored by the Dean of Students, and provide occasional input about issues that may impact students. For questions about the DAC, email Kellie Gerbers (kgerbers@westminsteru.edu). APPLY FOR THE DEAN’S ADVISORY COUNCIL Special Events Get connected with your fellow Griffins. Each semester, the dean hosts monthly events that are free to attend. Dean’s Challenge: Do you have what it takes? Challenge the Dean of Students in friendly, low-stakes competitions this semester. If you win, you get ultimate bragging rights, social media fame, and FREE swag. Game on! Biscuits with the Dean: Calling all Ted Lasso fans! Join the dean in the L.S. Skaggs Integrated Wellness Center kitchen to bake and enjoy “biscuits” (aka shortbread cookies) while chatting about what's on your mind.
